lesson: patch("pkg.mod.subprocess.Popen") does not scope the mock to the module under test. A module imported with `import subprocess` holds the shared module object, so patching its attribute replaces Popen for the whole interpreter — any unrelated subprocess.run() reached during the test picks up the MagicMock and fails unpacking communicate(). Symptoms surface inside CPython's own subprocess.py, which reads as an interpreter or version problem. Patch the name the module under test actually calls (patch.object on the imported function), not an attribute of a module it shares with everything else.
task: Diagnose a ValueError inside CPython subprocess that looked like a Python 3.14 incompatibility
validation: tests/test_mcp.py::test_manager_start_success failed with "ValueError: not enough values to unpack (expected 2, got 0)" at subprocess.py:557. Traceback showed the call entering manager._child_env -> install_openai_api_key -> credentials.resolve_openai_api_key -> subprocess.run, which had inherited the test's Popen mock. Confirmed by git-diffing _child_env before and after mq-agent #280, which added the credential call. Fixed by stubbing manager.install_openai_api_key

lesson: AtlasController.run() and finalize() returned an unannotated `str | dict`, so every `json_mode=True` caller was typed as a union. Pylance then resolved `state["outputs"]` against `str.__getitem__` and raised reportArgumentType at 14 call sites across 5 test files. The fix belongs at the source, not the call sites: three @overload stubs keyed on `json_mode: Literal[False] -> str`, `Literal[True] -> dict[str, Any]`, plus a `bool -> str | dict[str, Any]` fallback that the CLI needs because it passes a runtime `args.json`. Omitting the bool fallback overload breaks the CLI call site. Second, separate issue: mypy at default strictness only flagged the bare `self.calls = []` (var-annotated); it never saw the union-indexing problem, so mypy-clean does not imply Pylance-clean. Verify both — `python -m mypy` and `python -m pyright` (Pylance is pyright).

lesson: A `git pull` on a local branch that carries an unpushed commit will replay that commit on top of whatever was just merged, silently reintroducing content the merge was meant to remove. In atlas-core, `7c49c5b` (machine-local .mcp.json/.cursor/mcp.json) had been committed directly on LOCAL main and never pushed; the feature branch was cut from it. After dropping it from the PR branch via `git rebase --onto origin/main 7c49c5b <branch>` and merging, `git pull` on main rebased that still-local commit on top of the merge as a new SHA (2d9fddf), so local main had the files back while origin/main was clean. `git ls-files | grep ...` on the local checkout would have reported a problem that did not exist on the remote. Always confirm remote truth with `git ls-tree -r --name-only origin/main` or `git branch -r --contains <sha>`, and check `git reflog show main` to find whether a surprising commit is local-only. Recovery without data loss: `git reset --mixed origin/main` — the files stay on disk and, once gitignored, become invisible to status. Second point: `git merge-tree --write-tree` predicts a merge result without touching the working tree, and `git show <tree>:README.md` renders the merged file — use it to check a PR's real merge outcome instead of trusting the `mergeable` field, which reports UNKNOWN until GitHub recomputes after a base change.

After `git reset --mixed origin/main`, `git status -sb` showed `## main...origin/main` with no divergence and both files still present on disk but untracked and gitignored. lesson: Atlas Core's observation format is the load-bearing contract for evidence checking: every repo adapter (filesystem, github_reader, mqobsidian) emits "<relative path>:\n<content head>", so the citable source label is parsed from the first line that ends with ':' and looks like a path. mqobsidian prefixes a "Durable memory (not runtime truth...)" provenance line BEFORE the path line, so the parser must scan lines rather than assume line 1 — and durable memory must be excluded from the evidence base entirely, because docs/safety-model.md already states memory is context, not current runtime truth. Second, non-obvious design point: gating PASS on a boolean alone leaves quality_score meaningless (a repo_review citing nothing still scored 0.95, and an end-to-end "second iteration improves the result" test cannot assert score improvement). Making evidence a multiplier on the formatting score — factor = 0.75 + 0.25*coverage — makes the gate arithmetic: 0.95*0.75 = 0.71 falls below PASS_THRESHOLD 0.78 on its own, and the second pass at coverage 1.0 returns 0.95, so improvement is measurable. Third: adding fields to a schema with additionalProperties:false REQUIRES declaring them or every emitted document fails validation; keeping them out of "required" is what preserves 1.x compatibility.

lesson: In atlas-core the distinction that matters for the evaluator is citation vs verification, and names must not blur it. `cites_a_source()` only tests whether a finding names a file that was read — it never compares the claim against that file's contents — so a factually wrong statement mentioning README.md passes the gate. Two naming consequences, both caught in review: (1) the executor's retry section must be `## Observed sources`, not `## Verified findings`, because it attests that files were read, not that any repo defect was proven; (2) `RouteEvaluator` needs `evidence_heading` (where an output records what it read) separate from `finding_headings` (where it makes claims that must name a source) — collapsing them makes the gap code lie about what is checked, which is why `no_findings_cited` was renamed `sources_not_documented`. Also: `evidence_coverage` must be None, not 1.0, when an output asserts no finding — 1.0 reads as a perfect score for having said nothing. Rule of thumb for this repo: a heading, field, or gap code is part of the contract; if it promises more than the check performs, that is a defect even when every test is green.

lesson: Two design points worth keeping. (1) A failing ModelAdapter must NOT fall back to the rule-based executor — serving a deterministic template as though a model produced it is a false success, the same failure class the P1 evidence gate exists to prevent. Fallback is only correct when no adapter is configured; those are different situations and the API contract now distinguishes them. (2) To exit with a meaningful code, the CLI cannot read stop_reason out of the text trailer — docs/api-contract.md forbids inferring completion semantics from prose. The fix is structural: cli.py always calls run(json_mode=True) and renders text from that document via finalizer.render_run_text(), so text and --json share one implementation and cannot drift. Exit map is 0 passed / 1 failed / 2 no_actionable_retry+max_iterations / 3 approval_required, kept total against typing.get_args(StopReason) by a test, so a new stop reason forces an explicit decision instead of silently hitting the catch-all. Also: do not fake timeouts. execute() is synchronous, the core cannot cancel an in-flight call, and a thread wrapper only stops waiting while the request keeps running — so the contract assigns the deadline to the adapter, which is the only layer that can enforce it. Blast-radius note: .github/workflows/run-atlas.yml pipes atlas through tee, so a non-zero exit is masked by the pipeline status and the workflow was unaffected.

lesson: Three non-obvious things. (1) Putting validation in a classmethod factory like Observation.create() leaves a hole: dataclasses.replace() calls __init__ directly, so it will write a malformed digest or a blank provenance field into an object that already looks validated, and will keep a derived source_id that no longer matches the path it names. Validation belongs in __post_init__, which also lets you re-derive and reject a mismatched source_id so an observation cannot be silently re-pointed. (2) A snapshot id derived from (root, commit, worktree_state) cannot detect a dirty->dirty content change: the worktree stays dirty at the same commit, so has_moved() returns False while the file has changed. The roadmap asked for "ändrad HEAD/fil under läsning", which needs a state check AND a per-source content check — detect_drift() pairs them. Verified by hand before writing the fix. (3) Hash the FULL file content, never the excerpt, and keep the excerpt plus its line range as separate fields. That way bounding or later redacting the excerpt cannot move the identity that verification compares — which is what makes P0.1c's secret redaction safe to add on top. Verification must check both digest and line range: the digest alone misses an excerpt that no longer matches the lines it claims. Also: UNKNOWN must be declared `UNKNOWN: Final = "unknown"` or mypy rejects it as a default for Literal-typed fields.

lesson: Redaction must happen on export, never at collection, and the reason is concrete: verify_observation compares the stored excerpt against the lines it claims in the file, so a masked excerpt stops matching and an untouched source verifies as "stale". Keep raw excerpts local (the roadmap's "råa källor förblir lokala") and build a masked view in the manifest. Assert in tests that constructing the redacted view moves neither content_sha256 nor the verification verdict, or the ordering can regress silently. Path containment: resolve symlinks BEFORE the containment check, and use Path.relative_to rather than a string prefix — "/tmp/root-evil" startswith "/tmp/root" but is a different directory. Refuse escapes with an exception rather than clamping the path, since silently reading a different file than requested is worse than failing; allow symlinks that stay inside, because the rule is about where bytes come from. Redaction patterns must be narrow (credential shapes, home dirs, email) or they cut away the context needed to check a claim — validate both directions: zero matches across the repo's own files (no false positives) and confirmed matches on the test fixtures (positive control). Finally, an export manifest should omit the absolute snapshot root, which names a user and a machine; snapshot_id identifies the state without it.

lesson: The load-bearing design for P0.2: make `verified` structurally unreachable from the deterministic layer rather than merely avoided by convention. check_finding() can establish a citation is sound (source_id exists in this run, claimed digest matches the observation, source still verifies fresh, quoted text sits contiguously at the claimed line range) — and none of that shows the source supports the claim, so a sound citation returns insufficient_evidence and a broken one contradicted. Assert the guarantee three ways: never construct the literal in code, add a test that greps the module for `verdict="verified"` / `return "verified"`, and have apply_to() downgrade a self-asserted verdict so a producer writing verdict="verified" onto its own finding is overruled (the roadmap's "modellens eget självomdöme får inte ensamt ge PASS"). Second point: EvidenceRef must carry what the finding CLAIMS about a source and be checked against the run's observations — never copied from them, or every citation is trivially correct and the check is theatre. Third: verifying a quote requires contiguity at the claimed range, not substring presence; a cherry-picked excerpt assembled from real lines elsewhere in the file must fail, which a plain `in content` check would pass.
